fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of what I know comes from building systems rather than coursework. The work most relevant to Palantir is probably my job-application agent, a local Playwright and TypeScript system where I used SQLite as the single source of truth because browser automation gets dangerous when application state can diverge across processes. Every application moves through an explicit state machine, every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags that never default on, and free-text and demographic fields are architecturally prevented from being auto-filled. I also built a validation ladder so a capability isn't called working just because it passed against a local fixture. Separately, I build the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital, including the ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so analysts can act on the output. The theme across both is that I care about where automation should stop, not only where it can go.

items.question: Additional information
items.problem: Expected "I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of what I know comes from building systems rather than coursework. The work most relevant to Palantir is probably my job-application agent, a local Playwright and TypeScript system where I used SQLite as the single source of truth because browser automation gets dangerous when application state can diverge across processes. Every application moves through an explicit state machine, every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags that never default on, and free-text and demographic fields are architecturally prevented from being auto-filled. I also built a validation ladder so a capability isn't called working just because it passed against a local fixture. Separately, I build the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital, including the ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so analysts can act on the output. The theme across both is that I care about where automation should stop, not only where it can go."; page shows "(empty)"
